scenes.title: Nakano Broadway shopping arcade side streets
scenes.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create an ORIGINAL, richly painted 16-bit pixel-art environment atlas for a Japanese driving game. Reference image 1 is STYLE ONLY: match its intricate architectural detail, colorful warm windows, textured roofs, luminous atmosphere and hand-placed pixel clusters. Do not reuse its buildings, landmarks or composition.

Image layout: exactly FOUR equal-height full-width panoramic strips stacked vertically, no margins, no borders, no captions, no letters labelling seasons. Preferred canvas 1536 x 1920 pixels (each panorama 1536 x 480); all four images fill their entire strip. Each strip depicts EXACTLY THE SAME camera, building silhouettes, storefront widths, windows, utility poles and perspective; only foliage, snow, weather and seasonal light change. Top to bottom SPRING, SUMMER, AUTUMN, WINTER. Never combine two seasons within one strip. All strips aligned on precisely the same architectural geometry.

District subject: Nakano Broadway shopping arcade and its surrounding narrow side streets in Tokyo, NOT Nakano Sunplaza. A dense horizontal urban composition: left, layered crooked low-rise shops with a comic/book store, old record shop, tiny noodle bar, striped awnings and outdoor display cabinets; center, the tall rectangular mid-century concrete Broadway complex with long bands of small windows above a glowing deep shopping arcade entry, crowded small vertical shop signs and shallow side alleys; right, an inviting low-rise side lane opening between a tile-roofed izakaya and a weathered blue-gray apartment block with balconies, roof water tanks and utility wires. The arcade is the visual anchor but not centered symmetrically. View the street frontage mostly straight-on from across the avenue, with just enough recession in side lanes. Two cherry trees and dense planter vegetation break up the facades. Make the architecture materially varied, individually drawn and credible, with tiny crates, shutters, vending machines, exposed pipes, grills, antennas, rich tile and concrete texture, a few readable modest Japanese shop markings but NO large headings or image labels.

Spring strip: pink cherry blossom foliage, pale rosy evening sky, soft warm shop light.
Summer strip: lush green trees, clear blue-cyan late-afternoon sky, bright golden shop windows.
Autumn strip: red-orange foliage, peach amber evening sky, amber reflections and warm interiors.
Winter strip: leafless branches and light snow on roof edges, awnings and planters, icy pale violet sky, warm interiors.
All buildings and landmarks must be fully redrawn consistently in all four strips. Horizon architecture reaches the very bottom edge of EACH strip, only a narrow pavement lip at bottom. NO foreground road, NO vehicles, NO prominent foreground people, NO UI, NO labels, NO poster montage, NO giant plain geometric placeholder blocks. Render polished original game background art, nuanced shading and layered fine pixel detail everywhere.

scenes.title: Arai Yakushi temple shopping lane
scenes.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create an ORIGINAL richly painted 16-bit pixel-art environment atlas for a Japanese driving game. Reference image 1 is STYLE ONLY: match its finely textured hand-painted pixel architecture, luminous warm shop interiors, clustered foliage, delicate windows and sophisticated rich palette. Do not copy its buildings, Nakano Sunplaza, shopping arcade gate, or composition.

Layout: exactly FOUR equal-height full-width panoramic strips vertically stacked, flush edge to edge, no margins, no borders and absolutely no season captions. Preferred canvas 1536 x 1920 pixels, four 1536 x 480 panoramas. Every strip has precisely identical camera, building shapes, roof geometry, window locations and street layout. Only tree foliage, snow and seasonal illumination change. Top row SPRING; second SUMMER; third AUTUMN; bottom WINTER.

District: Arai Yakushi temple shopping lane in Nakano, Tokyo. A unique low-rise old-neighborhood composition different from a downtown skyline. Left third: a substantial traditional Buddhist temple entrance with a dark curved ceramic tiled roof, timber pillars, a copper-green hanging lantern, stone lanterns and a view inward toward another temple roof; an ancient spreading tree rises behind it. Midground center: the shopping lane mouth is a narrow gap between intimate two-story wooden tea and rice-cracker shops with paper lanterns, baskets and warm glass counters, small Japanese shop plaques and potted plants. Right third: a varied row of old neighborhood businesses including a florist with buckets and a tiny kissaten with a rust-colored awning, one weathered cream three-story apartment with tiny balconies behind them. Dense power lines, mossy wall sections, layered roof tiles and ceramic details establish lived-in Nakano. Composition mostly broad side-on frontal street elevation across an unseen road, no large vanishing-point road and no empty foreground. Highly individual hand-painted architectural forms, roof ridges, slats, window grids, patterned noren curtains, aging stucco, gutters, signs, meticulously shaded textures. Rich detailed background neighborhood roofs visible between large branches. Temple and modest street shops share the panoramic frontage.

Row 1 SPRING: flowering cherry trees in soft pink, tender leaves, rose-and-gold late-afternoon light.
Row 2 SUMMER: broad deep green shade trees, flower-shop hydrangeas, turquoise-blue sky and warm sunlight.
Row 3 AUTUMN: blazing vermilion and gold maple canopy, scattered leaves on eaves, soft golden sky.
Row 4 WINTER: bare branches, light fresh snow delicately defining roofs and stone lanterns, pale lavender sky and warm glowing windows.
Architecture remains identical across all four seasonal strips, with seasonal changes integrated into the actual artwork rather than overlays. The buildings, temple wall, shops and plants meet the very bottom edge of each strip; only a thin sidewalk edge. NO foreground roadway, cars, scooters, bicycles, large people, text labels, UI, picture frames, watermarks or crude geometric abstractions. Expert-level original pixel-art scenery, intricate and atmospheric, worthy of a polished commercial game.

GAME COMPOSITION: shallow frontal side-on panoramic environment viewed across an unseen road. Background architecture/landscape should extend to the BOTTOM edge of EACH strip. At most a hairline pavement lip, NO blank foreground ground plane and NO foreground road. Keep enough detailed architecture in the lower half for visibility behind gameplay. Exquisite roof tiles, boards, brickwork, stone, aged plaster, balcony railings, gutters, tiny detailed shopfronts or relevant landscape details. Strong silhouette design and layered depth, never crude abstract rectangular placeholder shapes. Finely drawn environmental storytelling, deliberately varied materials. Small contextual Japanese sign marks acceptable; no large words. NO large foreground people, vehicles, cars, UI, text overlays, watermarks, or season labels.

DISTRICT COMPOSITION:
NAKANO SUN MALL GATE: A frontal street panorama anchored on the LEFT by a wide rounded shopping-arcade entrance whose arched translucent pink-and-cream canopy carries repeating semicircular ribs far into a deep illuminated passage. The central band is a lively covered fresh-food market frontage with checkerboard awnings, hanging lanterns, fishmonger display cases and colorful vegetable bins; to the RIGHT is a tall narrow corner coffee building with a wraparound glass mezzanine and old record shop underneath. Behind them smaller offset tiled rooftops, a chunky exterior staircase, ornamental lamps, telephone cables and tiny roof gardens, not a skyscraper downtown skyline. The entrance must be much wider and lower than the tall red Broadway block, pink arches are the main motif. Two small deciduous street trees in planters provide seasonal contrast. No temple, no Sunplaza triangle, no centered symmetrical building.

Final check: exactly FOUR aligned season strips, each has the SAME district geometry, no season labels, summer trees green, architecture and landscape reach each panel’s bottom edge.
